start_here: Say to your AI: "From my recordings in /Work/demo/recordings.json, which I and the speaker agreed to, pick the cleanest stretch of continuous speech to clone the voice from, using my settings in /Work/settings.json." It runs tool:pick-the-cleanest-speech-to-clone-from on your computer and gives you the best windows.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it reads a recordings file on your computer and writes candidate wavs and reference-candidates.json into a folder you name.
instructions: 1. Install ffmpeg, numpy, scipy and soundfile; write your settings file (this tool reads reference_lufs_min and reference_lufs_max).
2. List only recordings of the person who agreed to be cloned: {"recordings":[{"clip","source","words":[{"text","start","end"}]}]}.
3. Say "Pick the cleanest speech to clone from". Your AI reads the row with tools:list and runs its run command with your recordings file, your settings and a new output folder.
4. Read the printed best windows (signal to noise, loudness, text) and pass the best wav and its text as reference and reference_text to tool:clone-speech-that-repair-could-not-fix.

worked_examples.title: The first unbroken stretch of a synthetic recording becomes the reference
worked_examples.ask: Pick the cleanest stretch of this speaker's recording to clone their voice from.
worked_examples.given: Run here for real on the test fixture's clean.wav (a synthetic voiced tone with word times alpha 0.5-0.9, bravo 1.0-1.5, charlie 2.4-2.9, delta 3.0-3.4, echo 4.4-4.9) and test/settings-for-synthetic-speech.json. The recordings file /Work/demo/recordings.json holds that one recording. The script's default window is ten seconds, which this 5.6 s file cannot fill (it would answer best: []), so this run added the script's own flag --window 1.0, which the row's run line does not pass. The AI reads the row with this tools:list call, then runs: python3 trillion-workshop/tools/grade-and-repair-speech-audio/do-work/choose_clone_reference.py --recordings /Work/demo/recordings.json --settings /Work/settings.json --out /Work/demo/ref --window 1.0. Paths shown for /Work/demo/ref.
worked_examples.hands_back: It prints "/Work/demo/ref/clean_0.50.wav snr 29.1 lufs -14.75 tail None | alpha bravo" (the first run of words with no pause over 0.4 s lasting one second: alpha then bravo, cut from 0.50 s) and the last line {"result": {"candidates": "/Work/demo/ref/reference-candidates.json", "best": ["/Work/demo/ref/clean_0.50.wav"]}}.
